failure_modes: A time-conditioned ramp (C005/C006) displaces surrounding non-landmark coordinates, increasing noncore squared displacement and strain with no demonstrated affinity benefit.
Selecting a dose-only change (C001/C003) alters injection RMS without any time-conditioned evidence, and the incumbent already matches C002/C004, so it is not a supported edit.
Treating the observed coordinate contrast curves or their temporal derivatives as physical interaction energies or as a spatial gradient would misstate the reward semantics.
Presenting last-record survival credit or nearest-teacher distance as final affinity benefit, when no decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied.
rationale: D1.2: The registered alternatives split into a dose-only knob (native_rms_ratio C001/C002/C003) and a time-conditioned ramp (time_ramp_power C004/C005/C006). The incumbent already sits at native_rms_ratio=0.33 (C002) and time_ramp_power=0.0 (C004), so the only genuinely time-conditioned option is a ramp power edit, which under the temporal_region recipe changes regional attention at observed score nodes while keeping the same static teachers and the same shared FLOWR endpoint. That is a coordinate/attention change, not a teacher-coordinate change and not a velocity force; the observed curves are coordinate contrasts, and a temporal derivative is not a spatial gradient. D4.1: The evidence does not supply a defensible expected advantage for any offered edit. The observed support is the learning window [0.0,0.5] with 50 observed score times, and the curve-support rule retained 24 features under a fidelity rule; the continuous contrasts show sign changes and rate reversals with no accepted polynomial, so a constant rule is unsupported but so is any specific ramp exponent. The information audit states the geometric nearest-teacher comparison is not the full score-weighted reward or its FLOWR Jacobian, and teacher score correlations are observational, not a validated affinity predictor. No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied, so no realized affinity benefit can be claimed for a ramp. Because the objective is affinity-first and the evidence gives no expected advantage, retaining the incumbent is the defensible choice; the evidence would change this decision only if a validated contrast showed a consistent, non-conflicting sign over the observed window with a decoded affinity endpoint. D4.2: The concrete failure response I predict for a time-conditioned ramp is unnecessary displacement of surrounding coordinates: a ramp that grows the regional attention weight late in the window would pull non-landmark neighbors along with the attended region, raising noncore squared displacement and strain without a demonstrated affinity gain, and could push cumulative RMS toward the 6.0 A constraint. That prediction is why I do not select C005/C006; a coordinate graph change alone is not treated as a failure mechanism, and no temperature, resampling, affinity-head derivative, extra model forward or graph-equality restriction is proposed.
